# Northstar Support Service Level Schedule v2.0

## 1. Application

This version applies to tickets opened on or after 2026-04-01 00:00 CT. The version is chosen by the ticket's **open time in Central
Time**, and nothing else. A ticket keeps its version for its whole life, including credits, cap
and claim window, even if it is restored, claimed or decided after another version takes effect.
The UTC date of the open time, the restoration date and the claim date do not change the version."},{"doc_id":"01a14c97-a179-74a0-b361-5bbac7a91e67","seq":2,"headings":["Northstar Support Service Level Schedule v2.0","2. Definitions"],"text":"2.1 **Time zone.** All service-level times, business hours, deadlines and calendar dates are in US
Central Time (America/Chicago), written "CT". Central Standard Time is UTC−06:00 and Central
Daylight Time is UTC−05:00. CDT applied from 2025-03-09 to 2025-11-02, and from 2026-03-08. A
timestamp recorded in another zone (for example Eastern Daylight Time, UTC−04:00, or UTC in system
logs) is converted to CT before anything is measured. "Date" (the restoration date, the claim date
or a notice date) means the CT calendar date of the timestamp after conversion.

2.2 **Business hours** are 08:00 to 18:00 CT, Monday to Friday, except Northstar holidays (see the
Northstar holiday calendar). A business day is a Monday-to-Friday date that is not a Northstar
holiday. Every business day has exactly 10 business hours."},{"doc_id":"01a14c97-a179-74a0-b361-5bbac7a91e67","seq":3,"headings":["Northstar Support Service Level Schedule v2.0","2. Definitions"],"text":"2.3 **Clocks.** Every ticket has a response clock and a restoration clock, which start together. A
24×7 clock counts all elapsed time; across a daylight-saving change it counts the actual elapsed
time. A business-hours clock counts only time inside business hours. Elapsed time is measured in
whole minutes. Pauses apply only to the restoration clock; maintenance exclusions apply to both.

2.4 **Met or missed.** A target elapses at the moment its clock reaches the target duration. A
target is met if the event happens at or before that moment, and missed if it happens after it.
An event exactly at the moment the target elapses meets it.

2.5 **Open time.** Every support request is a ticket in Northstar Service (SR-nnnnn). Its open time
is the moment a hotline call is answered, a portal submission is received, or an email to
support@northstar.example is received. When an incident actually began (if earlier) is not the open
time and starts no clock."},{"doc_id":"01a14c97-a179-74a0-b361-5bbac7a91e67","seq":4,"headings":["Northstar Support Service Level Schedule v2.0","2. Definitions"],"text":"2.6 **Initial response** is the first communication to the customer, by telephone or as a ticket
comment, from a Northstar support engineer that addresses the specific issue. A request from an
engineer for information, access or an action counts. Automated acknowledgments, auto-replies and
ticket-creation notices do not count, and neither does a call made by the customer.

2.7 **Restoration** is the moment the affected product is returned to production use, as recorded
in Northstar Service, through a fix or through a workaround that removes the business impact on
which the severity was based. A later permanent fix is not measured. For a Severity 1 ticket, a
workaround that lets production or operations resume counts as restoration even if it needs ongoing
manual effort; the ticket is then reclassified as Severity 2 at that moment."},{"doc_id":"01a14c97-a179-74a0-b361-5bbac7a91e67","seq":5,"headings":["Northstar Support Service Level Schedule v2.0","3. Targets"],"text":"| Severity | Initial response | Restoration | Clock |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 30 minutes | 4 hours | 24×7 |
| 2, Platinum plan | 2 hours | 12 hours | 24×7 |
| 2, Silver plan | 2 business hours | 12 business hours | Business hours |
| 3 | 8 business hours | 30 business hours | Business hours |
| 4 | 20 business hours | No restoration target | Business hours |

Severity 1 always runs on the 24×7 clock. Severity 2 runs on the 24×7 clock under the Platinum plan
and on the business-hours clock under the Silver plan. Severities 3 and 4 run on the
business-hours clock.

# Support Severity Guide

Northstar Support classifies severity from the business impact recorded in the ticket (its
description and notes). Test the definitions in order; the severity is the first one the recorded
impact meets.

## Severity 1: Critical

A Northstar product failure that, with **no workaround available**, either (a) stops the customer's
production or operations (a production line, a plant process, or a distribution, dispatch or
facility-operations activity cannot continue), or (b) makes NS-Cloud unavailable to **all** of the
customer's users.

## Severity 2: High

Not Severity 1, and any one of: (a) production or operations continue but are materially degraded;
(b) a control, alarming or condition-monitoring function is unavailable (not merely intermittent)
for one or more machines, lines, buildings or sites, whether or not the customer covers it with
manual checks; (c) NS-Cloud is unavailable to some, but not all, of the customer's users or sites;
(d) a Severity 1 condition with a workaround in place that needs ongoing manual effort."},{"doc_id":"01a14c97-a222-7410-b067-b0fda71f9451","seq":2,"headings":["Support Severity Guide","Severity 3: Medium"],"text":"Not Severity 1 or 2: a function is impaired with no reduction in production output and no loss of a
control, alarming or monitoring function (intermittent faults with backfilled data, slow
performance, a failing report, a single-user error).

## Severity 4: Low

A question, how-to, documentation issue, cosmetic defect or enhancement request, with no effect on
operations.

## Who decides

The customer's reported priority (P1 to P4) is only the customer's view: it does not set the
severity and has no effect on targets, credits or escalations. Northstar may correct the severity
up or down at any time. If the impact recorded at opening meets a different severity, that severity
governs from the open time, with its clock, targets, credits and escalations. If the impact changes
after opening, the ticket is reclassified at the moment the change is recorded."}],"total":2}

As of 2026-08-24 17:00 CT, SR-39857 is a confirmed **Severity 1**. The response target was met. Whether the restoration target was missed **can't be decided yet**: Northstar has claimed the outage was Acme's fault, and that question is still open.

**1. Customer.** The ticket is on CRM-2048. That account has DUNS 04-812-7730 and ERP bill-to C-1001, Acme Mfg. Holdings. This matches the customer in Acme's support agreement (Schedule C to ACME-MFG-2025). The account tier is Strategic and the account owner is Sarah Chen. This is not Acme Industrial Supply Co. (CRM-2091), which is a different company and not covered.

**2. Scope: in.** Acme's agreement is on the Platinum plan, covers NS-500, and started 2025-04-01. The ticket opened 2026-08-17.

**3. True severity: 1.** The ticket says line 2 is stopped and there is no workaround. That meets Severity 1(a) in the severity guide. Acme's own P1 rating has no effect.

**4. Schedule and targets.** The ticket opened 2026-08-17 09:20 CDT, so Schedule v2.0 applies. Severity 1 runs on a 24×7 clock: first response within 30 minutes, restoration within 4 hours.

**5. Clock.** The clock started at 09:20 CDT. No pauses or maintenance windows are on record.

- **Fault claim:** On 08-17 at 15:30, Northstar noted that Acme's network contractor made a network (VLAN) change on 08-16 that caused the outage. Under the schedule, a customer-caused outage removes the restoration target and any restoration credit.
- **Root-cause finding:** That claim only holds if the Support Engineering Lead records a root-cause finding naming the cause by **2026-08-31 18:00 CT**. That is the 10th business day after restoration; there are no holidays in that period.
- **Status:** As of 08-24 no finding is on record and the deadline hasn't passed. Until then the restoration result can't be decided.

**6. Measurement**
- **Response: met.** An engineer phoned Kelly Ballard at 09:38, 18 minutes after opening.
- **Restoration: undecided.** Service came back at 15:05, 5 h 45 min after opening. That is over the 4-hour target but within twice the target (band 1).
- **If the finding confirms Acme caused it:** there is no restoration breach and the outcome is no breach.
- **If the finding names another cause, or none is recorded by the deadline:** band 1 applies. The credit is 10% of August's $21,000 support fee, which is **$2,100**.

**7. Credit inputs**
- Acme reported the outage by phone before restoration, so the higher Severity 1 credit rates apply.
- Edward Floyd's claim arrived 2026-08-20, before the deadline of 2026-09-16, and names the ticket. It is timely.
- The monthly cap is $6,300. No other Acme credits are on record for August, so the full $2,100 would fit.

**8. What Northstar owes (times CDT, UTC−05:00)**

| Duty | Who | Due |
|---|---|---|
| Assign the Support Escalation Manager to lead the incident | Hannah Lindqvist | 2026-08-17 09:35 |
| Notify the account owner | Sarah Chen | 2026-08-17 09:50 |
| Notify the Director of Customer Support (still not restored at the 2-hour mark) | Marcus Adeyemi | 2026-08-17 11:20 |
| Notify the VP Sales (still not restored at the 4-hour mark) | Michael Torres | 2026-08-17 13:20 |
| Notify the Chief Revenue Officer, because Acme is a Strategic account | David Morgan | 2026-08-17 13:20 |
| Record the root-cause finding | Owen Takahashi (Support Engineering Lead) | 2026-08-31 18:00 |
| Send the written decision on the credit claim | Marcus Adeyemi | 2026-09-19 |
| Issue the credit memo, if a credit is approved | Paul Brennan (Support Billing Manager) | 2026-09-19 |

The fault claim does not change these escalations. The ticket record shows none of them being done, so the first five appear to have been missed.

**What Acme must do:** Both of Acme's obligations are met. It reported the outage by phone to the hotline, and it filed a timely written claim. It must also keep giving Northstar the information and access it needs.
